items.title: Delhi High Court denies anticipatory bail to builder Nayan Raheja in money laundering case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday dismissed the anticipatory bail application filed by builder Nayan N Raheja in a money laundering case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Justice Amit Bansal rejected Raheja's anticipatory bail plea. A detailed order is awaited. ED is probing a case involving the alleged diversion of funds collected from homebuyers of projects developed by Raheja Developers. It is alleged that nearly ₹2,699 crore was collected from homebuyers, of which around ₹1,353 crore was allegedly diverted through various accounts, group entities and related transactions. The agency alleged that Raheja repeatedly failed to appear before investigators despite summons issued under Section 50 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and undertakings given before courts to cooperate with the probe. Senior Advocate Vikas Pahwa with advocates Sandeep Kapur, Manmeet Kaur, Irfan Muzamil, Jasmeet Singh, Rishabh Munjal, Priyal Jain, Kholi Rakuzhuro and Kunal Kochar appeared for Nayan Raheja. items.title: Delhi High Court rules it can execute commercial decrees below ₹2 crore if original suit was within its jurisdiction
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that it can execute a decree arising from a commercial suit even if the amount sought to be recovered is below its ₹2 crore pecuniary jurisdiction threshold, provided the original suit was within its jurisdiction [Ozone SPA Vs Co-incept] Justice Subramonium Prasad held that a court does not lose its jurisdiction to execute a decree merely because the decretal amount falls below its pecuniary threshold. " The contention that alteration in pecuniary limit of the court which passed the decree would also take away the power of such Court to execute the said decree cannot be accepted ," the Court observed. Justice Subramonium Prasad The ruling came in an execution petition filed by Ozone Spa Private Limited against Co-Incept Hospitality Private Limited and others, seeking enforcement of a ₹1.19 crore decree passed in July 2018. The dispute arose from a franchise agreement executed in December 2013, under which Co-Incept Hospitality was permitted to operate a gym, spa and salon under the Ozone brand at Rajouri Garden in Delhi. Sequels mostly work if the previous film possessed some internal logic to continue from. In Jailer 2, Rajinikanth returns as ‘Tiger’ Muthuvel Pandian, a retired warden who once terrorised inmates at Tihar jail. The film builds up to a face-off between him and Bodhi Kalpak (SJ Suryah). items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday suspended the 4-year-jail sentence of former Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin Thachankary in a disproportionate assets case [ Tomin J Thachakary v State of Kerala ]. Justice A Badharudeen pronounced the order on an application filed by Thachankary seeking suspension of his jail sentence until the High Court decides his appeal challenging the conviction. While allowing Thachankary's plea, the Court observed that, prima facie there was no error in the vigilance court's finding that he had acquired assets disproportion to his known income. However, considering that the sentence imposed on him was only four years, the Court held that it could be suspended by imposing appropriate conditions. It, thus, directed him to deposit 75% of the ₹30.84 lakh fine imposed by the vigilance court before he could be released on bail and to execute a bail bond of ₹5 lakh with two sureties within a further period of one week after depositing the fine amount. items.title: Homemaker’s household services cannot be ignored in accident compensation merely because she is over 70: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that while determining motor accident compensation, a homemaker’s unpaid household and caregiving services cannot be disregarded merely because she is above 70 years of age [Ganga Devi v Rajesh Kumar & Ors] . Justice Anish Dayal said that the assessment of compensation should not be founded upon stereotypes or assumptions that a person ceases to contribute merely by reason of having attained an advanced age. The Court warned against such prejudices and said that data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. “This Court is conscious that such contributions, particularly those rendered within the household and without monetary remuneration, are often overlooked or undervalued. However, the absence of a monetary consideration cannot operate to the advantage of the tortfeasor or diminish the compensation otherwise payable to the injured claimant,” the Bench ruled. items.title: Turning off light, lying on woman and pressing her mouth not attempt to rape: Patna High Court
items.summary: The Patna High Court recently held that entering a woman’s house late at night, extinguishing the oil lamp, lying upon her and smothering her mouth to stifle her cries does not amount to an attempt to commit rape [ Md Ainul Haque v. State of Bihar ]. Justice Sandeep Kumar held that in the absence of any overt act towards penetration, such acts fall short of Section 376/511 ( rape/attempt to rape ) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Consequently, the High Court set aside the four-year rigorous imprisonment awarded to the accused, one Md Ainul Haque, under Sections 376/511 IPC, reducing his substantive sentence to the period of about two and a half months already spent in custody. It, however, convicted him under Section 354 IPC ( outraging modesty ) and directed him to pay a fine of ₹25,000, ordering the entire amount to be handed over to the victim as compensation. Justice Sandeep Kumar The order comes in the backdrop of a similar controversial ruling by the Patna High Court earlier this year, where the court held that pressing a woman's breasts or unfastening her salwar string did not constitute an attempt to rape. items.title: Property acquired by Catholic priests after joining religious order belongs to society, not legal heirs: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court has held that properties acquired by Catholic priests after entering a religious order and undertaking religious vows belong to the religious society concerned and cannot be claimed by their legal heirs merely on the basis of their family relationship [ ABVM Vs Deiva Nayagan ]. A Division Bench of Justices N Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan passed the ruling while allowing appeals filed by a Catholic religious society against a district court order granting succession rights to the relatives of a deceased priest over fixed deposits worth ₹56 lakh. The Court held that the ownership of properties acquired during a priest's religious service must be determined in light of the obligations undertaken by the priest and the circumstances of the property's acquisition. " The legal consequence of such acquisition must therefore be determined in the light of the religious obligations undertaken by him and the institutional character in which those properties were acquired, rather than merely by the fact that the title documents stood in his individual name," the judgment said. items.title: Jammu and Kashmir High Court makes AIBE mandatory for advocates enrolled since 2009-10
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently made it mandatory for all advocates enrolled across the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 2009-10 to pass the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) to be entitled to practice law. Although the Bar Council of India (BCI) had made AIBE mandatory for law graduates from 2009-10 onwards, the requirement had not been formally implemented for advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court has now directed its implementation. A notification to this effect was issued by the High Court's Registrar General MK Sharma on October 10, 2026. The notification lays down that law graduates enrolled as advocates with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, who graduated in the academic year 2009-2010 onwards, must qualify the AIBE if they have not already cleared the examination. items.title: Explainer: Why buying power at Rs 37 per unit has sparked a political storm in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to purchase power for up to Rs 37 per unit has triggered a big political row, prompting criticism over whether it was a result of poor planning or corruption. This is the highest cost of power paid in Tamil Nadu’s history, and is highly unusual for almost any state discom in the country. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has cited an unexpected high demand amid a prolonged summer due to the El Niño phenomenon as the reason for the high cost. According to the Energy Resources Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar, the state’s peak power demand shot up by almost 30% from around 16,800 MW in October 2025 to nearly 21,700 MW this October – an additional requirement of nearly 5,000 MW. But the El Niño crisis has been felt across India, including the neighbouring south Indian states. Critics have compared the situation with that of Andhra Pradesh to question the lack of prior planning. Andhra Pradesh, too, is facing a surge in demand and had to resort to short-term power procurement deals. However, the state took measures as early as the first week of September.
